newsitem.title: USA: Edison settles Palo Verde nuke cost recovery.
newsitem.headline: Edison settles Palo Verde nuke cost recovery.

text.p: Edison International's Southern California Edison Co said Friday it reached agreement with consumer advocates on the recovery of its investment in the Palo Verde nuclear plant.
Edison is a 15.8 percent minority participant in the 3,700 megawatt Wintersburg, Ariz., nuclear facility, which is operated by Arizona Public Service Co.

Under the agreement, Edison is entitled to recover the balance of its sunk investment in Palo Verde by December 31, 2001, earning a return of 7.35 percent, consistent with recently enacted state legislation.

Under the state plan, California's electricity market will be completely open to competition by January 2002, and investor-owned utilities have until then to depreciate investments made under the current system of regulated monopolies.
The sunk cost part of the agreement is nearly identical to a previous agreement on Edison's San Onofre nuclear plant, in which it is majority owner and operator, an Edison spokeswoman said.
But the recovery of incremental operating costs for Palo Verde will be based on "pass-through" of actual costs, rather than fixed per-kilowatt-hour costs as in the San Onofre settlement.
This "recognizes that we are the operator at San Onofre, and only a minority partner in Palo Verde," the spokeswoman said.
The San Onofre agreement also included incentives for Edison to meet certain operating and cost criteria.

With the Palo Verde settlement, state regulators can step in to perform a reasonableness review if actual incremental costs exceed the baseline forecast by 30 percent, or if the capacity factor for all units falls below 55 percent, Edison said.
The Palo Verde settlement also provides for Edison customers to receive 50 percent of the benefits of post-2001 operations, consistent with similar criteria for San Onofre.
